lesson_title: Catchment Management: The Fish Tank That Turned Green
hook_text: One act of kindness killed every fish in the tank. The same mistake is killing South Africa's dams.
clip_script: A classroom keeps a fish tank, and over the holidays someone doubles the feeding to be kind. The uneaten food dissolves and the water quietly turns rich. Algae wake up to a banquet and multiply until the water is opaque green. Below the green ceiling it is midnight, and the oxygen-making plants on the bottom die in the dark. Then the algae themselves crash, and the rot begins. Rot is done by bacteria, and bacteria breathe: decomposition strips the oxygen out of the water. The fish hang at the surface gulping, and by the end of the week the tank is still. Scale that tank up to a dam and you have eutrophication — feed, bloom, dark, die, rot, suffocate.
visual_style: Close-up of fish food swirling into clear water, water clouding green shot by shot, then a drone pull-back revealing a scummed South African dam, six beat-words punching on screen: FEED, BLOOM, DARK, DIE, ROT, SUFFOCATE.
pacing: Gentle start, tightening cuts through the six beats, dead-still water on the final frame.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to master the whole chain and the programme that repairs the damage.
